title: He died for sin…
paragraphs:
He died for sin…
But you’re still hiding it.

You say, “God hates sin, not sinners.”
But you whisper it like a defense… not a surrender.
Because there’s something you haven’t brought into the light.

Something hidden.
Something you justify.
And it’s eating you alive.
Let’s not pretend.

You can quote Scripture.
You can lift your hands in worship.
You can smile in church.

But there are nights—
when conviction gets louder than your excuses.
And suddenly, that phrase doesn’t comfort you anymore.
It confronts you.
Because here’s the tension:

If God hates sin…
and sin lives in you…
Then what does that mean for you?
We try to separate it.

“I made a mistake.”
“I’m just human.”
“It’s not that bad.”
But sin is not a harmless habit.
It’s treason against a holy God.

It corrupts what was created for glory.
It twists desire.
It blinds the heart.
And the most dangerous part?
You can get used to it.
You stop feeling it.

At first, it convicts you.
Then it whispers.
Then it becomes normal.

And what once broke your heart…
becomes something you protect.
That’s where many are right now.
Not far from God.
Just numb.
The Bible doesn’t soften this.
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?” — Jeremiah 17:9
That means your greatest enemy isn’t out there.
It’s in here.

Your heart can convince you that darkness is harmless.
That compromise is safe.
That you’re still in control.
But you’re not.
And here’s the weight of truth:
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
Not just physical death.

Spiritual death.
Separation.
Emptiness.
Distance from the presence of God.
Sin doesn’t just break rules.
It breaks you.
Because this is where everything shifts.
God doesn’t expose your sin to shame you.
He exposes it to save you.
Read this slowly:
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Not after you fixed yourself.
Not after you cleaned your habits.
Not after you became worthy.
While you were still in it.

Still hiding.
Still struggling.
Still failing.
Christ stepped in.
This is the collision point of eternity:

God’s hatred for sin…
and His love for sinners…
met at the cross.
Jesus didn’t die to make sin acceptable.
He died to make sinners redeemable.

Every lie you believed.
Every secret you buried.
Every compromise you excused.
He carried it.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

Not partially.
Not selectively.
Fully.
And here’s the part that breaks pride:
You cannot save yourself from what you secretly love.
That’s why repentance is not just behavior change.
It’s surrender.
It’s saying:

“I don’t want to protect this anymore.”
“I don’t want to justify this anymore.”
“I don’t want to hide this anymore.”
It’s turning.

Not just from sin—
but toward a Savior.
Because forgiveness is not found in effort.
It’s found in a Person.
Jesus Christ.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
Did you see that?
Not tolerate.
Not ignore.
Cleanse.
You don’t have to carry this anymore.

Not the guilt.
Not the shame.
Not the double life.
But you do have to come into the light.
This is the moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Now.
Ask yourself:
What am I still protecting that Jesus already paid for?
Let it go.
Lay it down.
Bring it into the open before God.
Because God doesn’t cancel sinners.
He transforms them.
You are not too far gone.
You are not too dirty.
You are not too late.
But don’t twist grace into permission.
Grace is not a cover for sin.
It’s power to be free from it.
So come.

Not polished.
Not perfect.
But honest.
And watch what Jesus does with a surrendered heart.
If this hit you—don’t ignore it.
If this stirred something deep in you…
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
